newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold, platinum group end higher with bullion.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold, platinum group end higher with bullion.

text.p: Tokyo gold and platinum group metal futures ended higher on Monday, buoyed by overnight gains in bullion prices and yen weakness, traders said.

They noted that gold continued to find support overseas from short covering by speculative funds, while ongoing concerns about delayed Japan-Russia supply contract talks buoyed palladium and pulled up platinum in its wake.

TOCOM most-active December gold settled 2 higher at 1,379 an ounce, the bottom of the day's 1,386 to 1,379 range. The nearby months showed particular strength, rising 10 yen, while the other months rose 2 to 5 yen.
The nearby months were lifted by short covering ahead of Tuesday's expiry of the spot contract, traders said, but in the other months individual investors sold at the early highs.
Bullion ended at $352.80/10 an ounce, up from Friday's close at $351.90/40 in New York and $350.60/90 in Tokyo.
Traders said a spurt of bullion buying, apparently from U.S. investors covering short positions, buoyed prices.

TOCOM December palladium ended 17 higher at 543 per gram, after earlier rising the 21-yen daily limit. TOCOM December platinum ended up 11 at 1,446 yen per gram, while the other months were 12 to 19 yen higher.
Continued concerns about Russian supplies of palladium continued to support prices, traders said.
Only silver bucked the firmer trend, with benchmark TOCOM December settling 1.6 lower at 205.8 yen per 10 grams.
Traders said TOCOM precious metals retraced from their early highs as the yen rebounded against the dollar.
Spot market sources added that physical demand for gold in Japan had dried up since a bullion rally late last week.
Finance Ministry data released this morning showed Japan's gold imports fell in 1996 to their lowest level since 1983.
